source: Ample Guitar M Main Panel Manual; the manual names middle C as C3, so its C0 is MIDI 24. Range 40-84 and the Palm Mute keyswitch (26) were confirmed by rendering; the other numbers follow the manual with the same octave offset.

playable_range.note: E1-C5 in the manual; notes outside are silent

keyswitches.name: Palm Mute
keyswitches.note: lower velocity of the played note = deeper mute

keyswitches.name: Slide In & Slide Out
keyswitches.note: press before a note = slide in, press while a note sounds = slide out; reverts to sustain

keyswitches.name: Legato Slide
keyswitches.note: then play two overlapping notes; reverts afterwards

keyswitches.name: Hammer-On & Pull-Off
keyswitches.note: then play two overlapping notes; reverts afterwards

controls.name: String force
controls.note: 31 = 6th string ... 36 = 1st string. A note that cannot be played on the forced string stays silent, so avoid these unless intended.

controls.name: Position assign
controls.note: press, then a note 40-56 selects the fret position

controls.name: Auto legato
controls.note: high velocity = automatic slide, low = automatic hammer-on/pull-off

controls.name: Open string first
controls.note: high velocity on, low velocity off

controls.name: Position mode
controls.note: low velocity = melody mode, high velocity = chord mode

tips: Articulation keyswitches latch and survive between renders: start every guitar track with an explicit keyswitch note (midi 24 for sustain) at time 0.
Place a keyswitch slightly before the first note it should affect (about 0.05 beat) and keep it short (0.1 beat).
Strum chords by staggering the chord notes 0.02-0.05 beat apart: low to high for a downstroke, high to low for an upstroke, with small velocity differences.
Use real guitar voicings (at most 6 notes, one per string); the default play mode enforces one note per string.
Pressing two articulation keyswitches together combines them: 24 + 26 gives sustain on loud notes and palm mute on soft notes.
